explanation: An expression referring to the restoration of Jerusalem, especially after the exile in Babylon.
Another designation for God, the almighty Creator and Sustainer of the universe.
To turn or change direction, here used concerning God's action of bringing His people back from exile.
An unavoidable event or situation, often linked to divine will or predestination.
A feeling of great happiness, here connected with Israel's reunification and rebuilding of their homeland.
A physical manifestation of sorrow or sadness, here used as a contrast to joy and laughter.
To plant seeds in the ground so that they grow into plants, here used as an image for labor and effort.
To gather crops after they have grown and matured, here used as an image for reward and success.
To hold or support something, here referring to carrying grain sacks as a symbol of the result of hard work and patience.
